meta.title: Rivian: The Car Works. Who Pays for the Loss?
meta.dek: The R2 outsold everything else Rivian makes in its first full quarter and the company raised guidance. The stock is 46% off its high anyway. What does $12 assume about the margin and about the share count?
meta.price_note: Oct 30, 2026 close, matched on Yahoo Finance and StockAnalysis
meta.type: Capital-intensive OEM (EVs) plus software and JV engineering services

verdict.sentence: The R2 is landing and the guide moved up, but $12.16 already needs the Bull: the probability-weighted five-year value is [[pw_ev]], a [[pw_return]] a year return against the 13% hurdle, because about 6% a year of share-count growth sits between revenue growth and value per share.
verdict.breaks_if: December does not exit at a positive automotive gross profit, which is also the condition for the first draw on the $4.5B DOE loan, or the next equity raise prices below $12.

call: Rivian printed its best quarter: 19,248 deliveries (+46%), revenue of $2.155B (+38%), the R2 outselling both the R1 and the vans in its first full quarter, and a guide raised on deliveries, EBITDA and capex. The market, at $12.16 after a new 52-week low of $11.45 the day before, is not pricing failure. It is pricing something near the Bull: to earn even 11% a year the stock has to reach about $20 by 2031, a dollar short of our $22 Bull, and the price implies **less than zero** Bear odds. We assign the Bull 25%. What the bull story leaves out is the bridge from the company to the share. In the Base, revenue compounds 10% to $12.5B at a 4% EBIT margin, yet about $6.5B of cumulative burn and about $0.84B a year of stock pay lift the share count from 1.46B to about 1.95B, leaving about $6 a share. This year's 220M new shares came 39% from a $15.50 public offering, 38% from partners and 23% from employees. The number that settles the page is Q4 automotive gross profit excluding credits, due in February; management says December will exit positive but not the full quarter. The verb is not probability-fragile: no Bear probability, even zero, clears 13% from here.

tests.claim: That funding stays strategic, not reflexive.
tests.test: through the Q2 2027 10-Q (early August 2027), no common or convertible offering below $12 outside the VW and Uber milestone agreements and employee plans, and a first DOE advance drawn. The stock closed at $12.16 on October 30.
tests.if_fail: Bear $2.00 → $1.50 and 5 points Base → Bear (PW EV $9.89, −4.1%/yr) → **Avoid / Exit**.

return_math.price_implied: At 11% a year the stock must reach about $20.5 by 2031 (12.16 × 1.11^5), which needs the Bull (≈$18B of revenue at a 9% EBIT margin). Even with no Bear at all, the Bull-and-Base mix is worth $11.65.
return_math.epv: n/m: earnings power is negative. Book value is ≈$3.9 a share (equity $5.7B ÷ 1.46B), so about 70% of the price pays for growth. The Bear sits below book because it is a dilution case.
return_math.base_rate: Revenue of $7.7B puts Rivian in the $7–12B bucket, where 3.6% of companies grew sales at least 20% a year in real terms for five years and 7.6% at least 15% ([`compounding.md`](../../frameworks/compounding.md)). The Bull's ≈18.5% nominal (about 16% real) is plausible but rare; the Base's ≈10% nominal (about 7.5% real) is probable, with Normal's capacity already built. Tiers: Bull plausible, Base probable, Bear probable.
return_math.terminal_growth: n/m on EPS. On EBIT, the Bull's 25× and the Base's ≈27.5× imply perpetual growth of about 6.7% and 7.2% at an 11% discount rate, above the 5.0% Treasury. Both still grow double digits at year five, so the multiple carries runway that the growth levers have to deliver.
return_math.year_ten: Still growing at year ten in the Base (Georgia phase one, R3), but thin margins mean the terminal multiple, not the earnings, does the work.
return_math.rr_note: The ratio is near 1:1 and the downside is dilution, not just a lower multiple: the Bear sits 84% below spot.
return_math.note: Computed rows come from model.json; terminal values are equity value per share set outside the engine (Bull EV 25× EBIT, Base EV 1.1× sales, Bear a dilution case), so EPS-based diagnostics are not defined. EPV, base rate and year ten are the author's. Built with Claude.
